topic: Reframing the identity narrative around overthinking
body:
**If you've been told you're "too sensitive" or "too in your head" — that's not a diagnosis. That's someone not having the language for what you're experiencing.**

There's a significant cost to internalising that kind of feedback. When you're repeatedly told that your thinking style is a problem, you don't just change the thinking style — you start to second-guess whether you can trust your own perception at all.

That self-doubt doesn't reduce overthinking. It creates more of it. Because now the question isn't just "was that conversation okay" — it's also "and can I even trust my read on whether it was okay."

The more accurate framing is this: you have a nervous system that is highly attuned. That attunement was useful at some point — possibly very useful. The pattern that formed around it is what's costing you, not the sensitivity itself.

Understanding the difference between the trait and the pattern is important. The trait doesn't need to be removed. The pattern can be changed.

You're not too much. Your nervous system learned something. And learned things can be updated.

Full explanation in the guide — link in my bio.
